headline: The RSM Classic: Marco Penge wins four-man sudden-death playoff for maiden PGA Tour title
teaser: Englishman Marco Penge claims his first PGA Tour crown on the first extra hole after a four-way tie at 16-under 266 in Monday finish at Sea Island.
story:
England Marco Penge delivered a career-defining breakthrough on Monday, 23 November, sinking a clutch putt on the first sudden-death playoff hole to win The RSM Classic at Sea Island Golf Club.

Sunday weather delays pushed the closing holes of the FedExCup Fall finale to Monday morning on the Seaside Course. Penge rallied with a final-round 65 to finish regulation locked at 16-under-par 266 alongside China Haotong Li, American Michael Thorbjornsen, and Max Greyserman.

Returning to the 18th hole for the four-man playoff, Penge seized the moment to collect his first career PGA Tour victory and a $1,332,000 winner share. Next on the calendar is Tiger Woods Hero World Challenge at Albany, Bahamas from 3 to 6 December.
whyCareReason: Penge captures a $1,332,000 winner check and locks in his PGA Tour exemption after weather pushed Sea Island final round into Monday.
stakes: The FedExCup Fall finale concludes with Marco Penge securing full PGA Tour membership and top-125 cards settled for 2027.
rivalryAngle: Intense head-to-head leaderboard scrap between young PGA Tour University graduates and seasoned European tour qualifiers.
funFacts: Sunday weather forced a Monday tournament conclusion for the second straight week on the PGA Tour.
Four players deadlocked at 16-under 266: Marco Penge, Haotong Li, Michael Thorbjornsen, and Max Greyserman.
Penge took home $1,332,000 for his maiden PGA Tour victory on the first playoff hole.
